comment:
The hillside, deck and trails are right; the Six Giant Rocks read as round silos (straight vertical sides, flat banded tops). They are the photograph's foreground, so make them real boulders:
1. Each rock an irregular, lumpy mass: wider at the middle than at the base, sides bulging and undercut, tops domed and uneven (not flat, no horizontal stripes), different heights (6 to 18) and shapes, two leaning against each other with a dark crack/gap between, one tall split rock. Weathered sandstone colours mixed in irregular patches, not bands: smooth sandstone, sandstone, cut sandstone, terracotta, light gray terracotta, a little tuff and granite at the base, moss carpet and moss blocks in the hollows on top, a few ferns and grass growing out of cracks.
2. Settle them into the slope: their bases sunk into the ground on the uphill side, the ground built up around them with coarse dirt, rooted dirt and stone so none sits on the grass like a placed object.
3. Put a few people-free details on the deck: the chain-or-fence railing all along its outer edge, two benches, and three warm lanterns on posts.
Keep the terrain, the deck's position and height, the trails and the open north-west view exactly.
summary: Replaced the old boulder code in parts/rocks.mjs with lumpy rocks: narrow at the foot, bulging in the middle, uneven domed tops. Heights run from 7 to 18; R2 leans onto R1 over a dark slot, R5 leans north-west, and R3 is split by a 1-wide cleft. Colours are irregular patches with no bands; there is moss on the tops and ferns or grass in 9 cracks. Bases are buried uphill, reach down to the ground everywhere, and sit in a mound of coarse dirt, rooted dirt and stone. A diff against v1 shows only the rock area changed; the check finds nothing floating and no orphans.
applied: 1. Irregular boulders: each layer is a wobbly ellipse that shifts with height. They bulge in the middle, are narrow at the foot and end in uneven domes. Heights are R1 16, R2 12, R3 18, R4 11, R5 16, R6 7.
1. Leaning pair: R2's top shifts 4 west onto R1's shoulder, with a dark 1–2 wide slot below. R5 also leans north-west.
1. Split rock: R3 (the tallest) has a 1-wide cleft from the fourth layer up, and its east half is 4 lower.

1. Colours in irregular patches, with no horizontal bands (the brown bedding band is removed): smooth sandstone, sandstone, cut sandstone, terracotta, light gray terracotta and a little orange terracotta. The bottom layers mix tuff, granite and terracotta, with moss on the north side. Moss blocks and moss carpet sit in patches on the tops, more on the north side. 9 vertical cracks on the north and west faces each have a fern or grass at the foot. I added cut_sandstone, light_gray_terracotta and granite to palette.json.

2. Settled into the slope: each rock starts at the bottom of its area, so the uphill side is buried in the hill. Where the ground is lower, the base reaches down to it. A mound of coarse dirt, rooted dirt, stone and some moss surrounds every foot: 1 high downhill, 2 uphill. It stays off the trails and out from under the deck.

3. Deck: the fence railing around the outer edge (with the trail gaps open), the two north-facing benches and the warm lanterns on fence posts were all already there and are unchanged. The lanterns are 5 corner lanterns plus 10 more that keep the deck too bright for mobs to spawn.
skipped: The deck has more than three lanterns. I didn't cut them down to three because the extra 10 are what keep the deck from spawning mobs at dusk.
The palette check flags light gray terracotta as clashing with the blocks around it. I kept it because you asked for it.
The plan's rule that the gap between R1 and R2 stays open air all the way up is now broken, because R2 leans onto R1 as you asked.
